title: Closure Query Receipt
$comment: The result of asking one sealed BoundedClosure about one exact canonical target state (DESIGN-compile-before-query §3, §7). A query supplies the target's canonical bytes; presence requires the bytes AND the digest to occur together (a digest match with unequal bytes is refused as corruption, not answered). Presence returns a shortest replayable native action sequence; absence returns NOT_REACHABLE_WITHIN_HORIZON, never plain 'impossible' — the receipt names the snapshot, horizon, visited-state count, closure digest, and native verifier so the bounded negative can never be quoted without its bound. Human-selected targets are a demonstration, not scored evidence: the closure predates them, and nothing here carries a score.

outcome.$comment: CORRUPT_TARGET is the digest-matches-bytes-differ refusal. There is deliberately no 'IMPOSSIBLE' member: this vocabulary cannot express an unrestricted negative.

shortest_route.$comment: Canonical action strings, present exactly when outcome is REACHABLE; replaying them through the world's own verifier from the initial state must reproduce the target bytes.
